blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — promethazine pediatric contraindication
stem: A provider prescribes promethazine injection for an 18-month-old child. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer a reduced weight-based dose and closely monitor respiratory rate and oxygen saturation afterward.
options.B: Hold the medication and clarify the prescription because use in children younger than 2 years is contraindicated.
options.C: Administer the prescribed dose if the child has no history of sleep apnea or other respiratory disease.
options.D: Give the medication with another antiemetic so a smaller promethazine dose can be used for symptom control.

rationale: Current PHENERGAN injection labeling lists use in pediatric patients younger than 2 years as a contraindication because of the risk of respiratory depression. The boxed warning and pediatric respiratory-depression warning report postmarketing cases including fatalities in this age group. Therefore the nurse should hold the medication and clarify the prescription. Dose reduction, absence of preexisting respiratory disease, or combining promethazine with another antiemetic does not remove the age-based contraindication.
educational_objective: Recognize that promethazine injection is contraindicated in children younger than 2 years because of the risk of potentially fatal respiratory depression, requiring the nurse to hold and clarify the prescription.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: DailyMed updated June 30, 2025; prescribing information revised December 2023; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Boxed Warning — Respiratory Depression in Pediatrics; Contraindications; Warnings — Respiratory Depression, Pediatrics; Pediatric Use.
source_claim_supported: PHENERGAN injection is contraindicated in pediatric patients younger than 2 years because of respiratory depression risk; fatal respiratory depression has been reported in this age group.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; administer medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Specified the injection formulation to align the stem exactly with the authoritative label.
Rewrote all four choices as plausible medication-safety actions of comparable length while retaining one age-contraindication response.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B is uniquely correct because the current label explicitly contraindicates promethazine injection below age 2; the alternative monitoring and dose-adjustment strategies cannot override the contraindication, and the original length cue is removed.
